Ben Zoma's own logical argument for why this first immersion is required even for one already ritually pure, reasoning by analogy from the five service-changing immersions between sacred locations to the mundane-to-sacred transition of entering the courtyard, with a forward cross-reference to the chapter's own later derivation (32a) (l28); and Rabbi Yehuda's competing explanation that this initial immersion is merely a formal gesture with no independent Torah obligation, meant to remind the High Priest to search his own conscience for any forgotten impurity before serving (l33).
